The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

OpenAI IPO won't happen this year, says Sam Altman. "Given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public," OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Fortune. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin Suisse plans to cut up to half its Swiss jobs as it shifts work abroad. The company is closing its Copenhagen IT site while maintaining Bratislava and opening a new hub in Vietnam to reduce costs. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Nigel Farage’s Reform UK lands $97 million donations from two crypto billionaires in 24 hours. The combined haul equals the largest individual political donations in U.K. history, sharply scaling up crypto industry backing. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Anthropic CEO calls for AI race to slow down citing safety. Musk and OpenAI's Altman agrees. Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Elon Musk have agreed on an unusual position: frontier AI development may need to slow as systems become capable of helping build their own successors. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ripple stablecoin chief sees $13 trillion corporate treasury opportunity for RLUSD. Payments and capital markets are driving growth for Ripple's $2.4 billion digital dollar as it looks to bring RLUSD to Europe under MiCA, the firm's Jack McDonald said. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ditching bonds for bitcoin: How crypto can tackle the AI-heavy portfolio dilemma. Bitcoin Suisse says rising AI investment, government debt and weakening stock-bond diversification strengthen the case for adding bitcoin to traditional portfolios. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $77,012 with a -0.36% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,510.81 with a -0.64% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: BTC and ETH ETF Inflows Slam 9-Day Winning Streak
items.description:
Wu Blockchain reported on August 28, 2026, that US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $242M and spot Ethereum ETFs took in $235M on August 27, with both categories logging nine consecutive days of inflows.

The synchronized run traces back to August 17, when both categories began climbing together. It continued uninterrupted through August 27. These bullish inflows have fuelled the rally across the crypto markets over the past ten days. [...] 99bitcoins

# BTC and ETH ETF Inflows Slam 9-Day Winning Streak

Alex Ioannou

3 min read

 BTC-USD

  -1.04%
 ETH-USD

  +0.33%
 SOL-USD

  -0.91%
 HYPE32196-USD

  -2.87%

In Bitcoin ETF news today, BTC traded near $79,500 on August 28, up +1.1% over 24 hours, as US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) posted $242.30M in net inflows on August 27, extending their streak to nine consecutive trading sessions. [...] The scale gap between the flagship categories and the smaller funds is stark. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, IBIT, contributed $209M of a $338M Bitcoin ETF inflow on August 24.

Its Ethereum fund, ETHA, added $90.92M of that day's $116 million Ethereum ETF haul. Those figures exceed the combined reported totals for Solana and Hyperliquid on August 27.

## Crypto ETFs Gain Traction as Rules Become Clearer

Regulatory momentum also lifted crypto ETFs. By October 2025, the SEC placed Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs under a generic listing standard, simplifying oversight and making institutional access easier.

Spot ETFs for Solana, XRP, and Litecoin joined the party in late 2025.2025 Crypto and Stablecoin-Key Events [...] Hassan Shittu

After years of opposition, the U.S. finally embraced crypto regulation in 2025.

The year 2025 proved to be a defining moment for the U.S. crypto sector. On July 18, President Donald Trump signed the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act, also known as the GENIUS Act, into law, creating the first comprehensive federal framework for dollar-backed stablecoins. [...] Still, progress toward clearer rules continued. In July 2025, the House passed the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act to define whether digital tokens fall under SEC or CFTC oversight.

After the ex-SEC Chair Gary Gensler resigned in January 2025, Acting Chair Mark Uyeda and the new SEC chair, Paul Atkins, pushed rules-based oversight, easing uncertainty and boosting ETF and digital asset growth.

items.title: GENIUS Act explained: What it means for crypto and digital assets
items.description: Signed into law on July 18, 2025, the historic legislation sets up a regulatory framework for USD-backed payment stablecoins and serves as a crucial first step towards broader digital asset regulatory clarity. While stablecoins are the main focus of the legislation, you’re likely to see effects across the entire digital asset ecosystem. That could mean tailwinds for crypto assets and crypto-related companies, as well as traditional financial companies that will bring their business on chain.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.
